match.reason: The bank card teaches the same partial fractions method but only for distinct linear and irreducible quadratic factors at Units 1 and 2 depth, while the Specialist Unit 3 point needs repeated factors and the integration and graphing use, which would require new steps rather than small changes.

draft.title: Partial fractions in Unit 3
card: A rational function whose numerator has lower degree than its denominator can be split into simpler fractions. If the denominator is (x − a)(x − b) with a ≠ b, then p(x)/((x − a)(x − b)) = A/(x − a) + B/(x − b).
To find A and B, multiply both sides by the denominator. This gives p(x) = A(x − b) + B(x − a). Then substitute x = a and x = b to remove one unknown at a time.
Example: (5x + 1)/((x − 1)(x + 2)). Then 5x + 1 = A(x + 2) + B(x − 1). Putting x = 1 gives 6 = 3A, so A = 2. Putting x = −2 gives −9 = −3B, so B = 3.
The split makes integration easy, because the integral of 1/(x − a) is ln|x − a|. So the integral of A/(x − a) is A ln|x − a|.
draft.remember: Split the fraction, find each constant by substitution, then integrate each part as a logarithm.

a.why: We need 3x + 5 = A(x + 2) + B(x + 1). Putting x = −1 gives 2 = A, and x = −2 gives −1 = −B, so B = 1. The swapped answer 1/(x + 1) + 2/(x + 2) mixes up which constant goes with which factor.
a.clue: Put x = −1 to find A, then x = −2 to find B.

b.q: What is the integral of 7/((x − 3)(x + 4)) with respect to x?
b.why: Write 7 = A(x + 4) + B(x − 3). Putting x = 3 gives A = 1, and x = −4 gives B = −1. So the fraction is 1/(x − 3) − 1/(x + 4), which integrates to ln|x − 3| − ln|x + 4| + c. Adding the logarithms ignores the negative sign on B.
b.clue: Split first, then check the sign of the second constant.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's example and both answers check out: 2/(x + 1) + 1/(x + 2) for (a) and ln|x − 3| − ln|x + 4| + c for (b).
